title: throughput-contracts-deferred-scaling-pacing-shaper
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a scalable policy component for Dedicated capacity that enforces per-tenant throughput contracts while smoothing reactive autoscaling via a deferred-scaling decision stage and an in-flight pacing shaper. The policy should compose target metrics (eg. sustained TPS, short-window token/sec spikes, 95th- and 99th-latency percentiles, concurrency) into a single scaling intent, apply a two-stage scaling algorithm (fast reactive adjustments + contract-aware reconciler), and enforce safety fences (burst budgets, cooldown curves, max-slew). The goal is to honor contractual throughput guarantees with predictable latency and bounded cost, reduce spurious flapping, and allow controlled temporary oversubscription using delegated burst credits.
acceptance_criteria: Define contract model: guaranteed TPS (committed), burst allowance, and latency SLAs per tenant
Policy computes a unified scaling intent every 10s using weighted metrics and outputs a capacity target
Deferred-scaling stage can hold an upward scale for up to 60s to observe stability signals before committing additional nodes
Pacing shaper reduces instantaneous token bursts by pacing request admission when in-flight tokens exceed thresholds
Safety fences: per-tenant max-slew of 2x current capacity in any 5-minute window, global cooldown 120s after scale-up, and emergency backoff on error-rate spikes
End-to-end integration tests demonstrating reduced scale churn on synthetic spike workloads (>=30% fewer scale events vs baseline) and maintained 95th-latency under SLA for steady workloads
Expose metrics and dashboards: target_capacity, pending_scale_decision, pacing_delay_ms, burst_credit_remaining, and safety_fence_tripped
Documentation and PRD with operational runbook and rollback steps
technical_notes: Target-metric composition: use normalized z-scores for TPS, token-per-second, concurrency, and percentile latency. Weighting to be configurable per project/tenant

Scaling algorithm: two-stage. Stage A (Reactive) uses a short-window EWMA+derivative to propose immediate delta. Stage B (Reconciler) runs on longer horizon to ensure contract obligations and cost constraints; final decision = reconcile(StageA, StageB, safety_fences)

Deferred-scaling: upward proposals enter PENDING_UP for configurable hold_duration (default 60s). If during hold the moving-average request rate decays below a decommit threshold, cancel scale-up. Down-scaling remains aggressive but bounded by min-capacity from contracts

Pacing shaper: token-bucket admission controller per-tenant with borrowable burst_credit. When burst_credit exhausted, ingress is paced and clients see backpressure or queued short-term buffering (configurable).
Safety limits: implement a per-tenant 'max_slew' parameter, global emergency cap, and transient-error backoff trigger to override StageA proposals
State persistence: use existing scaling-coordinator KV store for pending decisions and burst-credit accounting. Ensure idempotency and crash recovery semantics
Compatibility: fallbacks to legacy autoscaler when policy unavailable; expose feature flag to enable per-tenant policy rollout
implementation_steps: Proto: write a lightweight simulator to validate policy heuristics against synthetic workloads (spikes, sawtooth, gradual ramp)
Design API surface for policy module and decision events. Spec schema for scaling_intent and pending_decision objects
Implement StageA reactive estimator using EWMA + derivative and test locally
Implement StageB reconciler that considers contract commitments, cost budget, and forecast buffer
Integrate Deferred-scaling state machine with coordinator KV and implement hold/cancel logic
Build per-tenant pacing shaper with token-bucket and burst_credit accounting, integrate into ingress path
Add safety-fence enforcement and emergency backoff hooks tied to error-rate and latency anomalies
Create dashboards, alerts, and tracing hooks for decision path debugging
Integration tests and chaos injection (simulated node failures, delayed metrics) to validate safety behaviors
Rollout gating: canary on non-critical fleet, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, then broaden to more tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Enable policy for internal sandbox tenants (5% of traffic) behind feature flag
Phase 1 (monitored): Enable for small set of enterprise customers with committed contracts (10–20% traffic). Monitor burst_credit patterns and cancellation rates
Phase 2 (gradual): Expand to all Dedicated fleets with staggered ramp and automated rollback triggers
Fallback: automatic revert to legacy autoscaler if pacing_delay_ms > configured threshold for > 5m or if error-rate increases > 3x baseline
Post-rollout: collect cost delta and SLA-attainment report after 30 days
testing_plan: Unit tests for metric normalization and weighted composition
Simulator-based regression tests covering spike, steady, and oscillatory workloads
Integration test harness using k8s e2e to validate KV persistence and recovery semantics
Load test with synthetic tenants exercising committed TPS vs bursts and assert SLA and cost bounds
Chaos tests: node outage during pending_scale decisions to verify idempotent recovery
Runbook dry-run: simulate rollback and measure mean time to revert (< 5min target)
